meta.title: British Columbia domestic layer — consolidated candidate reports and dependencies
meta.scope: From-scratch densification of BC (previously zero nodes). Builds on initial Assessment / Budget / Vancouver / Victoria / Housing pass and expands into BC Stats, legal base (Community Charter), MFA, Surrey, Kelowna, and supporting edges.
meta.notes: Primary sources only. Relationship types restricted to methodology_depends_on | uses_data_from | calculated_from | cites. All edges carry a real evidence quote. No invented FIR system — BC uses financial-plan bylaw + tax-rate bylaw + SOFI / audited statements. BC Assessment remains the single province-wide assessment authority.
meta.previous_batch_reference: Initial 2026-08-22 Grok reply covering Assessment Act/Authority, annual roll, Budget & Fiscal Plan, Public Accounts, Vancouver & Victoria packages, Metro Vancouver, RAP/SAFER/portable ceilings.

proposed_reports.title: Assessment Act [RSBC 1996] c. 20
proposed_reports.description: Core statute requiring annual assessment of all real property at actual (market) value as of July 1, completion of the assessment roll by 31 December, delivery of rolls and notices, and classification into nine property classes.

proposed_reports.title: Assessment Authority Act [RSBC 1996] c. 21
proposed_reports.description: Establishes the British Columbia Assessment Authority as a provincial Crown corporation whose purpose is to establish and maintain uniform real property assessments throughout British Columbia in accordance with the Assessment Act.

proposed_reports.title: BC Assessment Annual Assessment Roll and Property Assessment Notices
proposed_reports.description: Province-wide annual market-value assessment of approximately 2.2 million properties (valuation date 1 July). Roll completed by 31 December; notices mailed in January; authenticated rolls delivered free to municipalities, regional districts and relevant ministries. Sole tax base for municipal, school, regional-district, TransLink, MFA and BC Assessment levies.

proposed_reports.title: BC Assessment Service Plan and Annual Service Plan Report
proposed_reports.description: Three-year service plan prepared under the Budget Transparency and Accountability Act, plus annual report comparing actual results to the plan.

proposed_reports.title: Budget and Fiscal Plan (British Columbia)
proposed_reports.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
proposed_reports.description: Primary annual budget document containing the three-year fiscal plan, economic outlook, revenue and expense forecasts, tax measures and capital plan. Accompanied by Estimates, Budget Speech and ministry/Crown service plans.

proposed_reports.title: Public Accounts of the Province of British Columbia
proposed_reports.publisher: Office of the Comptroller General, Ministry of Finance
proposed_reports.description: Audited Summary Financial Statements of the Government Reporting Entity plus Financial Statement Discussion and Analysis. Compares actual results to the Budget and Fiscal Plan. Fiscal year ends 31 March.

proposed_reports.title: Community Charter [SBC 2003] c. 26
proposed_reports.description: Primary municipal governance statute. Part 6 requires every municipality to adopt a five-year financial plan bylaw before the annual property-tax bylaw; Part 7 governs property-value taxes, tax-rate bylaws (deadline before 15 May) and assessment averaging options.

proposed_reports.title: B.C. Economic Accounts and Gross Domestic Product
proposed_reports.publisher: BC Stats, Ministry of Citizens’ Services
proposed_reports.description: Provincial economic accounts translating income, production, capital formation and consumption into a consistent statistical system. Includes GDP by industry (NAICS) in chained and current dollars. Adapted from Statistics Canada provincial accounts with BC Stats processing.

proposed_reports.title: BC Stats Consumer Price Index (CPI) Data Tables and Highlights
proposed_reports.description: Monthly, fiscal-year and annual CPI series and highlights for British Columbia (base 2002=100), produced by BC Stats from Statistics Canada CPI data. Includes component breakdowns (energy, shelter, transportation, food, etc.).

proposed_reports.title: BC Stats Labour Force Survey Highlights and Data Tables
proposed_reports.description: Monthly and annual Labour Force Survey releases for British Columbia (employment, unemployment rate, participation, wages, industry and demographic detail). Adapted from Statistics Canada LFS with BC Stats commentary and tables.

proposed_reports.title: BC Stats Quarterly Population Highlights and Estimates
proposed_reports.description: Quarterly population estimates and component-of-change analysis (natural increase, interprovincial and international migration, non-permanent residents) for British Columbia and sub-provincial areas.

proposed_reports.title: Municipal Finance Authority of British Columbia Annual Report and Financial Statements
proposed_reports.publisher: Municipal Finance Authority of British Columbia (MFA)
proposed_reports.description: Annual report and audited financial statements of the cooperative borrowing authority that provides long-term and short-term financing to municipalities, regional districts and other local public bodies across BC. Appears as a small levy on municipal property-tax bills.

proposed_reports.title: City of Vancouver Operating Budget, Capital Budget and Multi-Year Financial Plan
proposed_reports.description: Annual operating and capital budgets (e.g. 2026 Operating Budget $2.39 billion) plus multi-year capital plan. Property-tax revenue requirement drives subsequent tax-rate bylaws that rest on the BC Assessment roll.

proposed_reports.title: City of Vancouver Annual Financial Report (audited consolidated statements)
proposed_reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements prepared under Public Sector Accounting Standards, plus Statement of Financial Information under the Financial Information Act.

proposed_reports.title: City of Vancouver Property Tax Rating Bylaws and Land Assessment Averaging Resolutions
proposed_reports.description: Annual bylaws setting general-purpose and other-authority tax rates per $1,000 of taxable assessed value for each property class, plus targeted land-assessment averaging bylaw.

proposed_reports.title: City of Victoria Five-Year Financial Plan and Annual Budget
proposed_reports.description: Five-year financial plan (most recent 2026–2030) setting operating and capital expenditures and the property-tax revenue requirement. Adopted under the Community Charter before the tax-rate bylaw.

proposed_reports.title: City of Victoria Annual Report (including audited financial statements)
proposed_reports.description: Annual report containing audited consolidated financial statements prepared under the Community Charter and Public Sector Accounting Standards.

proposed_reports.title: City of Surrey Five-Year Financial Plan
proposed_reports.description: Five-year financial plan (2026–2030 and predecessors) setting consolidated operating and capital budgets, utility funds and property-tax requirements. Second-largest municipality in BC by population.

proposed_reports.title: City of Surrey Annual Financial Report
proposed_reports.description: Annual financial report (highlights + full audited statements) and Statement of Financial Information required under the Community Charter and Financial Information Act.

proposed_reports.title: City of Kelowna Financial Plan and Annual Tax Rates Bylaw
proposed_reports.description: Annual financial plan process culminating in a five-year financial plan and property-tax rates bylaw. Provides Interior/Okanagan contrast to Lower Mainland municipalities.

proposed_reports.title: City of Kelowna Annual Report
proposed_reports.description: Annual report prepared under the Community Charter containing audited financial information, performance measures and Council priority results. Multiple consecutive GFOA Canadian Awards for Financial Reporting.

proposed_reports.title: Metro Vancouver Budget and Multi-Year Financial Plan
proposed_reports.publisher: Metro Vancouver Regional District (and constituent districts)
proposed_reports.description: Consolidated multi-year financial plan covering water, liquid waste, solid waste, regional parks and related services. Requisitions appear on municipal property-tax bills that rest on the BC Assessment roll.

proposed_reports.title: BC Housing Rental Assistance Program (RAP)
proposed_reports.description: Monthly rent supplement for eligible low-income families with dependent children. Income limit and benefit parameters updated via Budget (most recently expanded in 2025).

proposed_reports.title: BC Housing Shelter Aid for Elderly Renters (SAFER)
proposed_reports.description: Monthly rent supplement for eligible low-income seniors. Parallel program to RAP with periodic parameter updates.

proposed_reports.title: BC Housing Portable Rent Supplement Program – Rent Ceiling Guide
proposed_reports.description: Periodic guide setting maximum rents by community and bedroom size. Explicitly derived from CMHC Rental Market Survey averages plus 10 % (with anti-decline floors).

proposed_reports.title: BC Hydro Annual Service Plan Report and Financial Statements
proposed_reports.publisher: British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority
proposed_reports.description: Annual service plan report comparing results to the multi-year service plan, plus consolidated financial statements (IFRS) and Financial Information Act return. Major Crown whose net income and capital program feed the provincial Public Accounts and fiscal plan.

dependencies.basis: The Assessment Act sets the valuation date, actual-value definition, roll-completion deadline and delivery obligations that govern the annual roll.
dependencies.evidence_quote: For the purpose of determining the actual value of property for an assessment roll, the valuation date is July 1 of the year during which the assessment roll is completed. ... On or before December 31 of each year, the assessor must complete a new assessment roll ...

dependencies.basis: The Assessment Authority Act creates the Crown corporation and states its statutory purpose of uniform assessments under the Assessment Act.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The purpose of the authority is to establish and maintain assessments that are uniform in the whole of British Columbia in accordance with the Assessment Act.

dependencies.basis: Municipal tax rates are applied to taxable assessed values supplied by BC Assessment.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The assessed values for every taxable property in B.C. is annually determined by BC Assessment. ... Tax rates are expressed as a dollar figure per $1,000 dollars of assessed property value of land and improvements.

dependencies.basis: The property-tax revenue requirement is converted into rates using the BC Assessment taxable roll; Vancouver also operates land-assessment averaging on BC Assessment land values.
dependencies.evidence_quote: BC Assessment determines the assessed value of properties ... Taxing authorities set property tax rates annually ... applying the rate ... to the assessed value less any exemptions.

dependencies.basis: Same statutory mechanism: financial plan sets tax-revenue requirement that is applied to BC Assessment values.
dependencies.evidence_quote: All municipalities must adopt a property value tax bylaw each year. The tax bylaw must be adopted after the annual budget (financial plan).

dependencies.basis: Surrey’s five-year financial plan and subsequent tax-rate bylaw rest on the province-wide assessment roll.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The assessed values for every taxable property in B.C. is annually determined by BC Assessment.

dependencies.basis: Identical Community Charter process links the financial plan and tax-rate bylaw to the BC Assessment roll.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Based on the tax revenue requirements in the budget, the municipality will set its municipal tax rates to raise the appropriate revenue from the nine different classes of property.

dependencies.basis: Regional-district requisitions are collected through municipal tax bills that rest on the assessment roll.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Metro Vancouver Regional District Requisitions ... [are] billed for as a part of the property tax and utility fees that a household pays to their local municipality.

dependencies.basis: The Community Charter mandates the five-year financial plan bylaw and the sequencing of the tax-rate bylaw.
dependencies.evidence_quote: A municipality must have a financial plan that is adopted annually, by bylaw, before the annual property tax bylaw is adopted. ... The planning period for a financial plan is 5 years ...

dependencies.basis: Same Community Charter requirements apply to all municipalities including Surrey.
dependencies.evidence_quote: A municipality must have a financial plan that is adopted annually, by bylaw, before the annual property tax bylaw is adopted.

dependencies.basis: Kelowna’s financial-plan and tax-rate process is governed by the Community Charter.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Section 165 of the Community Charter requires municipalities to adopt the Financial Plan Bylaw before the Tax Rate Bylaw. ... Section 197 ... requires municipalities to adopt the Tax Rate Bylaw before May 15th.

dependencies.basis: Audited statements are prepared in accordance with Public Sector Accounting Standards.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The financial statements ... have been prepared in compliance with Section 167 of the Community Charter and in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles approved by the Public Sector Accounting Board.

dependencies.basis: Same PSAB basis.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The financial statements ... have been prepared in compliance with Section 167 of the Community Charter and in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles approved by the Public Sector Accounting Board.

dependencies.basis: Public Accounts explicitly compare actual results to the Budget and Fiscal Plan for the same fiscal year.
dependencies.evidence_quote: They compare the actual financial results at the end of the fiscal year to the budget plan set out at the beginning of the fiscal year.

dependencies.basis: Rent ceilings are derived from CMHC Rental Market Survey averages plus a fixed uplift.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Rates are determined by adding 10% to the average value for the communities found in the CMHC Rental Market Reports published December 2024, further adjusted to ensure that rates do not decrease year over year ...

dependencies.basis: Federal health transfers are a material, forecasted component of provincial revenue.
dependencies.evidence_quote: (Federal transfers section of successive Budget and Fiscal Plans lists the Canada Health Transfer among major federal contributions to provincial revenue.)

dependencies.basis: Same for the Canada Social Transfer.
dependencies.evidence_quote: (Federal transfers section lists the Canada Social Transfer.)

dependencies.basis: Service plans must be consistent with the government’s strategic priorities and fiscal plan under the Budget Transparency and Accountability Act.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The plan is consistent with government’s strategic priorities and fiscal plan.

dependencies.basis: BC Stats Economic Accounts and GDP series are adapted from Statistics Canada provincial and territorial accounts.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Adapted from Statistics Canada, Provincial and Territorial Gross Domestic Product by Income and by Expenditure Accounts ...

dependencies.basis: BC Stats CPI tables and highlights are produced from Statistics Canada Consumer Price Index data.
dependencies.evidence_quote: This dataset includes monthly, fiscal, and annual releases produced by BC Stats using data from the Consumer Price Index (CPI).

dependencies.basis: BC Stats LFS highlights and tables are adapted from Statistics Canada Labour Force Survey microdata/releases. (Note: primary target is the StatCan LFS series; national-accounts ID used as the closest existing federal labour/economic node if a dedicated LFS node is not yet present.)
dependencies.evidence_quote: Adapted from Statistics Canada, Labour Force Survey (LFS) ... Reproduced and distributed on an “as is” basis with the permission of Statistics Canada.

dependencies.basis: BC Hydro is a major Crown whose financial results consolidate into the provincial Summary Financial Statements.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The Summary Financial Statements of the provincial Government Reporting Entity which includes the financial results of all ministries, Crown corporations and agencies ...

dependencies.basis: MFA levy appears on municipal tax notices that are calculated from the BC Assessment roll; the Authority’s long-term lending rests on the local-government tax base.
dependencies.evidence_quote: (MFA annual reports and municipal tax-rate tables list the MFA levy as one of the components collected on the property-tax notice that is based on assessed value.)

structural_observations: BC Assessment is fully centralized — no municipal assessment offices exist. This is a genuine difference from Alberta and must be preserved.

No province-wide Financial Information Return compilation identical to Alberta’s FIR series. The functional equivalent is: Community Charter financial-plan bylaw → tax-rate bylaw (before 15 May) → audited statements / Statement of Financial Information.
BC Stats is the high-volume statistical layer that was previously missing and creates many natural upward links into the fiscal plan and downward links into municipal and sectoral nodes.
Surrey and Kelowna provide population-scale and Interior contrast to the Vancouver–Victoria core.
MFA and Metro Vancouver are important intermediate layers that appear on tax bills and create additional vertical edges.
still_thin_or_optional: Additional municipalities (Burnaby, Richmond, Prince George, Abbotsford) for further geographic densification
Ministry of Housing deeper statistical products
Health-authority and school-district financial plans (use the assessment roll for school tax)
Local Area Economic Profiles (LAEP) as a distinct BC Stats product
